attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. The hedged 'might be... swindle' is set aside; the 'muddies the water' sentence is unhedged.

semantics.note: Faithfully gives the asserted effect of the policy sequence. Leaving out the hedged swindle judgment is correct.

contract.note: Reading 'muddies the water' as making available access harder to work out is an ordinary plain reading. Separating less access from less knowable access is fair.

evidence.note: Confirms the March 13–27 off-peak 2x promotion, which is the 'pumping' part of the sequence. Says nothing about whether access became harder to work out.
Peak-hour limits were announced March 26, overlapping the promotion's end. The order is off by about a day, but this does not refute the overlap and does not address whether access was knowable.
One unverified user report of confusion about the promotion. It predates the peak-hour change and does not isolate the cause.

reviews.rationale: The sequence is broadly confirmed: a promotion running March 13–27, overlapping peak-hour limits announced March 26. No before-and-after comparison or reproducible usage evidence shows that subscribers' access became harder to work out. The anecdotes do not separate policy effects from bugs. So the causal effect is not established either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unhedged sentence. The earlier 'I wager' governs a separate sentence.

semantics.note: Mostly faithful, but it drops the 'both to consumers and businesses' scope. 'Fail' is a looser word than 'do not work'.

contract.note: Calendar 2025 net loss of at least $2B per company is a fair reading of 'billions'. Treating 'no path' as no credible route at publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: Audited S-1 shows a 2025 Anthropic net loss of about $42B. Excluding the $34.3B fair-value charge, it is still several billion. Supports only the loss component.
Reports an OpenAI 2025 net loss of about $39B, or about $8B excluding a one-off charge. Supports only the loss component.

reviews.rationale: The loss component holds: both companies had 2025 net losses of several billion dollars on any basis reported. The packet has no evidence settling 'no path to profitability' or whether the products work at sustainable prices. The compound claim is therefore unresolved, with only its loss part supported.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unhedged assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Impossibility of ever' is a firm commitment that Anthropic never becomes profitable. The 'fundamental weakness' part is evaluative and not separately scored.

contract.note: Requiring a reconciled measure that covers costs is reasonable. But 'any kind' is broad, so whether an adjusted profit counts is an interpretation the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Secondhand report that Anthropic told investors it was profitable on an adjusted basis in Q3 2026. It is an undefined, unreconciled company claim, not independently verified.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The only counterevidence is an unreconciled adjusted-profit claim made by the company to investors and relayed by attendees. That does not meet the early-resolution rule, and no event supports the forecast. It stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'All evidence points to' is a firm inferential assertion, not a probability hedge. Reading it as GPU rental is consistent with the context.

contract.note: Measuring margins after operating costs and depreciation, in calendar 2025, is an ordinary reading. Refusing to treat adjusted EBITDA as profit is fair.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's 2025 operating margin was about -0.9% and its net margin about -22.7%. This fits the claim for one provider but is a consolidated result for a single company, not the sector.
CoreWeave's Q4 adjusted operating margin of 6% is still low. Its 57% adjusted EBITDA margin excludes depreciation. Quarterly non-GAAP figures for one firm.

reviews.rationale: The only data are CoreWeave's consolidated results, and they fit low or negative margins. The packet has no representative set of GPU rental margins across the sector, and the contract says one provider cannot settle the sector-wide claim. Unresolved.
